replies.What is your relationship with mathemati: Mathematics feels like a distant subject to me. I find it abstract and disconnected from my interests in chemistry or computer science. While I appreciate its logic, I don't enjoy the process of solving problems or understanding complex formulas. It's something I've had to study for exams but never truly embraced as a passion.
replies.Do you ever get anxious when thinking ab: Yes, absolutely. The pressure of getting it right and the fear of making mistakes makes me feel stressed. My moderate neuroticism scores mean I worry a lot, and math triggers that anxiety. I often avoid thinking about it unless necessary, preferring to focus on subjects I find more engaging.
replies.Did you ever use AI to support your math: I have used AI tools occasionally for quick explanations or checking my work. However, I found them sometimes too technical and not helpful enough for my needs. They didn't simplify concepts well, so I preferred traditional methods like textbooks or asking friends who understood the material better.

replies.Briefly, how do you perform a Principal: PCA involves standardizing your data first, then calculating the covariance matrix. Find eigenvalues and eigenvectors of this matrix. The eigenvectors with largest eigenvalues become your principal components. You project your data onto these new axes to reduce dimensions. Don't get anxious about it—break it down step by step like any other math problem.
